To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The cross sections for inclusive production of charged pions and eta mesons at 900 MeV/c are found to be consistent with the results of a previous experiment at the same momentum, and with the predictions from a Monte Carlo model.
The inclusive spectra of π and η at 90° are well described by a combination of perturbative QCD and hadronization models.

The production of charged particles at 90° is consistent with the scaling behaviour of the inclusive cross section, but with a different shape of the pT spectrum than the one predicted by perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics.

the study of high p T hadron production in pp collisions.
the production of particles at large transverse momentum, p T, in proton-proton collisions.
the study of particle production in the forward direction at the ISR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inclusive production of pions at 90° and the correlation measurements at 90° are consistent with the fragmentation model of the quark-parton picture.

1) the inclusive cross-sections for pions and eta mesons are consistent with a power-like behaviour in the range studied, and 2) the two particle correlation data are consistent with an independent particle picture.
(i) the inclusive cross sections are consistent with a power law behaviour of the type dσ/dpT ∼ pT-α, with α=6.8±0.2 for the π- mesons and α=6.4±0.2 (±0.2) for the π+ mesons (η mesons).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(a) the inclusive spectra are in agreement with a simple scaling picture, (b) the correlation function is consistent with a two-body phase space distribution of the type dN/dp1dp2 ∝ p1p2, (c) the correlation function does not depend on the pion transverse momentum p⊥, and (d) the correlation function has no azimuthal asymmetry.
